entries.test: Whether OpenAI's reported consumer (ChatGPT subscription) revenue in 2025 was smaller than its reported cash burn.
entries.note: The record widens "schoolchildren doing homework", a figure of speech, into all casual consumer use. His underlying claim is that consumer revenue cannot cover the burn.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI reaches about $200B in revenue by 2030, and whether its enterprise revenue grew throughout that period.
entries.note: He states continued enterprise revenue growth as a necessary condition for hitting the 2030 target.

entries.test: Whether Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey data available in early September 2025 showed AI use rates falling among large firms.
entries.note: "Hints" describes what the data suggests; it is not a probability statement. The post points to a decline among big companies over the prior two months.

entries.test: Whether documented enterprise GenAI deployments, such as those in the 2025 MIT study, include cases where returns did not cover costs.
entries.note: This is a weak existential claim ("not always"), so a few documented failures would confirm it.
"Can't help" is weaker than "are hurting", which is what the record says. Separating GPT-5's own effect on business demand is a counterfactual.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI fails (collapse, distressed sale, or insolvency) after its revenue stops growing.
entries.note: The antecedent ("things" stop going up) is loosely worded; revenue is the most plausible reading. There is no deadline.
